title: Acts Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Acts 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Saul breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples
Saul seeing a light from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Saul breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples
questions.explanation: Acts 9:1 states that Saul was yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, which is the earliest event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who did Saul go unto to get letters to Damascus?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:1 states Saul went unto the high priest to get letters to Damascus.

questions.question: What did Saul desire from the high priest?
options: Letters to Damascus to the synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: Letters to Damascus to the synagogues
questions.explanation: Acts 9:2 says Saul desired letters to Damascus to the synagogues.

questions.question: What happened to Saul as he came near Damascus?
options: A light from heaven shined round about him
questions.correctAnswer: A light from heaven shined round about him
questions.explanation: Acts 9:3 states that as Saul journeyed and came near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven shined round about him.

questions.question: What did the voice say to Saul?
options: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
Go to the city and wait
Fear not, I am with thee
questions.correctAnswer: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:4 records the voice saying unto Saul, 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?'

questions.question: Who did Saul ask when he heard the voice?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:5 shows Saul asking 'Who art thou, Lord?' after hearing the voice.

questions.question: What was the Lord’s reply to Saul’s question?
options: I am Jesus whom thou persecutest
I am the God of Abraham
I am the light of the world
questions.correctAnswer: I am Jesus whom thou persecutest
questions.explanation: Acts 9:5 states the Lord said, 'I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.'

questions.question: What did the Lord tell Saul to do after he was trembling and astonished?
options: Arise, and go into the city
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, and go into the city
questions.explanation: Acts 9:6 says the Lord told Saul to 'Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.'

questions.question: What was the reaction of the men journeying with Saul when they heard the voice?
options: They saw a man but heard no voice
questions.explanation: Acts 9:7 states the men journeying with Saul stood speechless hearing a voice but seeing no man.

questions.question: How long was Saul without sight after his encounter?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:9 says Saul was three days without sight.

questions.question: What was the name of the disciple in Damascus who received a vision from the Lord?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:10 states that there was a disciple at Damascus named Ananias who received a vision from the Lord.

questions.question: True or False: Saul was praying in the house of Judas when Ananias was told to go to him.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:11 says Saul was praying in the house of Judas when the Lord told Ananias to go to him.

questions.question: True or False: Ananias was hesitant to go to Saul because he knew Saul had done much evil to the saints at Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:13 shows Ananias expressing hesitation because he had heard how much evil Saul had done to the saints at Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord told Ananias to avoid Saul because he was too dangerous.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:15 says the Lord told Ananias to go to Saul because he was a chosen vessel, not to avoid him.

questions.question: True or False: Saul was given authority from the chief priests to bind all who called on the Lord's name.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:14 states that Saul had authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on the Lord's name.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Ananias say to Saul when he entered the house?
options: Brother Saul, the Lord sent me to heal you.
Saul, you have been chosen by God.
The Lord has commanded you to preach.
Saul, you must repent for your sins.
questions.correctAnswer: Brother Saul, the Lord sent me to heal you.
questions.explanation: This is correct as it reflects Ananias' greeting to Saul in Acts 9:17.

questions.question: What does Acts 9:18 promise will happen if someone receives their sight?
options: They will be filled with the Holy Ghost.
They will be healed of all diseases.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be filled with the Holy Ghost.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:17 states that Ananias said Saul would receive his sight and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: What fell from Saul's eyes when he received his sight?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:18 specifically mentions that scales fell from Saul's eyes when he received his sight.

questions.question: According to Acts 9:19, what did Saul do after he received meat?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:19 states that after receiving meat, Saul was strengthened and then preached in the synagogues.

questions.question: How did the people react to Saul's preaching in the synagogues?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:21 describes that all who heard Saul were amazed at his transformation and preaching.

questions.question: What did Saul do to confound the Jews in Damascus?
options: He proved that Jesus is the Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: He proved that Jesus is the Christ.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:22 indicates that Saul increased in strength and confounded the Jews by proving Jesus is the Christ.

questions.question: What was the Jews' plan against Saul after many days?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:23 states that the Jews took counsel to kill Saul after many days.

questions.question: How did the disciples help Saul escape from those who wanted to kill him?
options: They hid him in a cave.
They let him down by the wall in a basket.
They dressed him as a beggar.
They took him to the high priest.
questions.correctAnswer: They let him down by the wall in a basket.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:25 reveals that the disciples helped Saul escape by letting him down through the wall in a basket.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the disciples in Jerusalem when Saul tried to join them?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:26 states that when Saul came to Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid and did not believe he was a disciple.

questions.question: Who brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:27 mentions that Barnabas took Saul to the apostles and explained his encounter with the Lord.

questions.question: What did Saul do in the name of the Lord Jesus while in Jerusalem?
options: He spake boldly and disputed against the Grecians.
questions.correctAnswer: He spake boldly and disputed against the Grecians.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:29 indicates that Saul spoke boldly in the name of the Lord and disputed against the Grecians.

questions.question: Where were the brethren sending Saul to after they learned of the plot against him?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:30 states that the brethren brought Saul down to Caesarea and sent him forth to Tarsus.

questions.question: True or False: Saul initially faced immediate acceptance by the disciples in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as the disciples were afraid of Saul and did not believe he was a disciple (Acts 9:26).

questions.question: True or False: Ananias was instructed by the Lord to heal Saul.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Ananias was sent by the Lord to lay hands on Saul so he could receive his sight (Acts 9:17).

questions.question: True or False: Saul was alone when he encountered the Lord on the road to Damascus.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because while Saul was on the journey, the men with him stood speechless and heard a voice (Acts 9:7).

hard.title: Acts Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 9.

questions.question: What did the churches throughout Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria experience according to Acts 9:31?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:31 states that the churches had rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria.

questions.question: Who did Peter find in Lydda that had been sick for eight years?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:33 mentions that Peter found a certain man named Aeneas who was sick of the palsy.

questions.question: What did Peter say to Aeneas to heal him?
options: In the name of Jesus, be healed
Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed
Your faith has made you whole
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed
questions.explanation: Acts 9:34 records Peter saying to Aeneas, 'Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed.'

questions.question: What was the name of the disciple from Joppa who was full of good works?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:36 introduces a disciple named Tabitha, also called Dorcas, who was known for her good works.

questions.question: What did Peter do before he raised Tabitha from the dead?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:40 indicates that Peter kneeled down and prayed before turning to Tabitha and saying, 'Tabitha, arise.'

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people in Joppa when Tabitha was raised from the dead?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:42 states that it was known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord after Tabitha was raised.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'palsy' (παράλυσις) in Acts 9:33 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Palsy' in Acts 9:33 refers to a form of paralysis, consistent with the condition Aeneas suffered from.

questions.question: What literary device is present in the healing of Tabitha, where Peter raises her and presents her alive?
questions.explanation: The story of Tabitha uses inclusio, framing her death and resurrection to highlight Peter's authority and the power of faith.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of resurrection seen in Acts 9:40?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:22 recounts Elijah raising the widow's son, paralleling the resurrection theme present in Acts 9:40.

questions.question: Which Gospel passage correlates with the growth of the church in Acts 9:31?
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:19-20, where Jesus commissions His disciples, connects with the growth and multiplication of the church seen in Acts 9:31.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Acts 9:32?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:31 concludes with the churches being multiplied, which immediately precedes Acts 9:32.

questions.question: What comes immediately after Acts 9:38?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:39 follows Acts 9:38, describing how Peter was brought into the upper chamber where he prayed for Tabitha.

questions.question: The healing of Aeneas in Acts 9:34 demonstrates what aspect of Jesus' ministry?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:34 shows Peter invoking Jesus' name to heal Aeneas, demonstrating the miraculous power that was evident in Jesus' ministry.

questions.question: True or False: The churches in Acts 9:31 were in conflict and being persecuted.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:31 states the churches had rest, indicating they were not in conflict but were edified.

questions.question: True or False: Dorcas was known for her good works and almsdeeds.
questions.explanation: Acts 9:36 clearly states that Tabitha, also known as Dorcas, was full of good works and almsdeeds.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 9:16 teach about the relationship between divine calling and human suffering?
options: Divine calling includes a purpose for suffering in the believer's life
Suffering is unrelated to divine calling and is purely accidental
Divine calling guarantees immediate glory without suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Divine calling includes a purpose for suffering in the believer's life
questions.explanation: Acts 9:16 states, 'For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake,' showing that God’s chosen vessels are called to suffer as part of their mission.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 9:18 teach about the role of baptism in salvation?
options: Baptism is an immediate response following spiritual regeneration
Baptism is unnecessary for new believers
Baptism is a mere symbolic ritual without spiritual effect
Baptism replaces the need for receiving the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism is an immediate response following spiritual regeneration
questions.explanation: Acts 9:18 indicates Saul was baptized immediately after receiving sight and being filled with the Holy Ghost, illustrating baptism as a response to new life in Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about the sovereignty of God is taught in Acts 9:15 concerning Saul's role?
options: God sovereignly chooses individuals for specific redemptive purposes
Human will alone determines one's role in God's plan
Saul's role was accidental and not predestined
God limits His sovereignty by human opposition
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly chooses individuals for specific redemptive purposes
questions.explanation: Acts 9:15 describes Saul as 'a chosen vessel' for God to bear His name before Gentiles and kings, demonstrating divine sovereignty in election.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 9:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:4 features Jesus confronting Saul with knowledge of Saul's persecution, demonstrating God’s omniscience—His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 9:11 specifically demonstrate in the sending of Ananias to Saul?
questions.explanation: In Acts 9:11, the Lord directs Ananias in a vision to restore Saul’s sight, illustrating God’s providential care and guidance in salvation.

questions.question: How does Acts 9:20 connect to the broader New Testament theme of witness to the Gentiles?
options: It marks the beginning of Saul’s mission to proclaim Christ beyond the Jewish community
It restricts the gospel message exclusively to Jews
It emphasizes Saul’s rejection of Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the beginning of Saul’s mission to proclaim Christ beyond the Jewish community
questions.explanation: Acts 9:20 shows Saul preaching Christ boldly, preparing the narrative for his later extensive ministry to Gentiles, fulfilling the Great Commission.

questions.question: How does the deliverance of Saul in Acts 9:25 prefigure the Christian doctrine of divine preservation?
options: It illustrates God’s sovereign protection over His servants amidst persecution
It suggests believers are left defenseless against enemies
It shows that human effort alone secures safety
It denies the reality of spiritual warfare
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God’s sovereign protection over His servants amidst persecution
questions.explanation: Acts 9:25 depicts Saul’s escape by being let down in a basket, demonstrating God’s providential preservation of His chosen instruments.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 9:7 and Acts 9:8 teach about the nature of divine revelation and human perception?
options: Divine revelation can be perceptible audibly but not always visually to human companions
Divine revelation is always fully perceptible to everyone present
Human senses are infallible in detecting divine manifestations
Divine revelation never involves human sensory experience
questions.correctAnswer: Divine revelation can be perceptible audibly but not always visually to human companions
questions.explanation: Acts 9:7 shows the companions heard a voice but saw no one; Acts 9:8 shows Saul’s blindness, illustrating varying human sensory experiences during divine revelation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 9:26 and Acts 9:27 teach about early church reception of transformed sinners?
options: The church requires credible testimony and advocacy for accepting repentant sinners
The church immediately trusts every convert without question
Repentance is irrelevant for church membership
Transformation is denied by the church regardless of evidence
questions.correctAnswer: The church requires credible testimony and advocacy for accepting repentant sinners
questions.explanation: Acts 9:26 shows the disciples’ initial fear and distrust of Saul; Acts 9:27 shows Barnabas advocating for him, highlighting the church’s need for credible witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 9:34 and Acts 9:40 teach about the power of Jesus Christ in healing and resurrection?
options: Jesus Christ has authority to heal physical ailments and raise the dead through His apostles
Healing and resurrection are unrelated to Christ’s authority
Only Jesus Himself, not His apostles, can perform miracles
Miracles are purely symbolic and not real events
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ has authority to heal physical ailments and raise the dead through His apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 9:34 shows Peter healing Aeneas; Acts 9:40 shows Peter raising Tabitha, both by Jesus’ power working through apostolic ministry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Saul’s conversion account in Acts 9:3-7 is a hallucination and not a genuine divine encounter. What does Acts 9:3-7 actually teach?
options: Saul’s companions heard the voice but did not see Jesus, indicating an audible spiritual encounter
The event was a private psychological experience with no external evidence
Saul fabricated the vision for personal gain
The passage teaches that divine encounters are always seen by everyone present
questions.correctAnswer: Saul’s companions heard the voice but did not see Jesus, indicating an audible spiritual encounter
questions.explanation: Acts 9:7 states companions heard a voice but saw no man, affirming the reality of a supernatural auditory event rather than a mere hallucination.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 9:31 teach about the role of the Holy Spirit in the growth and unity of the early church?
options: The Holy Spirit provides comfort and fosters fear of the Lord, leading to church growth and edification
The Holy Spirit is irrelevant to church multiplication
Fear of the Lord hinders church growth
The church grows only by human effort without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit provides comfort and fosters fear of the Lord, leading to church growth and edification
questions.explanation: Acts 9:31 notes churches were edified, walking 'in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost,' demonstrating the Spirit’s essential role.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 9:15 demonstrate concerning God's election of Saul?
questions.explanation: God’s choice of Saul as 'a chosen vessel' in Acts 9:15 highlights divine sovereignty in electing individuals for His purposes.

questions.question: How does the restoration of Tabitha in Acts 9:40 contribute to the narrative arc of resurrection as a sign of the Messiah’s power?
options: It prefigures the ultimate resurrection power demonstrated by Jesus Christ
It contradicts the New Testament teaching on resurrection
It is an isolated event with no theological significance
It shows that resurrection power is limited to Peter only
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the ultimate resurrection power demonstrated by Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Peter raising Tabitha in Acts 9:40 foreshadows the resurrection power of Christ, affirming Jesus’ authority over life and death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 9:10 and Acts 9:13 teach about divine revelation and human obedience?
options: God reveals His will in visions, but human obedience may be hesitant due to prior knowledge and fears
Visions are always immediately obeyed without question
Divine revelation requires no human response
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His will in visions, but human obedience may be hesitant due to prior knowledge and fears
questions.explanation: Acts 9:10 shows the Lord addressing Ananias in vision; Acts 9:13 reveals Ananias’ hesitation due to Saul’s reputation, illustrating tension between revelation and obedience.
